- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +3+ points in 3-5 days), model often overshoots in next 5-10 days; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5 points.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.3–0.8 points to capture momentum.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply 0.5–1.0 point downward adjustment.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.8→0.0 or 0.4→0.0), model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days or reduce slope of price change.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price moving back toward 70–72 range), model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0 points above recent 10-day average.
